answer: Sortition should sample bonded coins, not account names. In a public stake graph, a vertex named willow or violet receives tickets only for coins exclusively locked to it. Draw five tickets independently, with replacement, after work is committed. Splitting one bond across a thousand new vertices preserves its total tickets, so a farm owning stake fraction p captures all five draws with probability p^5. Gaining more influence requires buying and locking more coins, incurring capital and financing costs.
